_about: Numeric transfer playbook. Prices are multiples of the in-game Transfer Value range: v_low and v_high are its bottom and top. Guaranteed = up-front + instalments. Calibrate from local/runs negotiation logs.

valuation._addon_weight: Add-ons count at this fraction of face value. 1.0 (user, 2026-10-08): they are usually hit, treat them as part of the fee. Offers are judged on value = guaranteed + addon_weight x add-ons (the offer page's 'Future & Potential Total Cost with Additional Fees').

selling._counters: Ask x v_high on the up-front fee, but at least min_raise_over_offer x their offer. Never accept a first negotiable offer.
selling._accept: Accept their reply once guaranteed >= this x v_high.

floor._floor: Walk-away minimum after max_counters: default and contract_under_12_months are x v_LOW; key_player is x v_high. Value includes add-ons.

selling._lowball: Guaranteed below this x v_low: reject rather than counter (a big jump lost Wrexham on 2026-07-01).
selling._non_negotiable: Accept-or-reject offers: accept when value (add-ons included) >= this x v_LOW, i.e. the bottom of his range (user, 2026-10-08: our floor sits below the value, not at its top).
selling._small_deal: Below this, handlers act automatically: one counter, then accept any reply >= v_low.
selling._asking_price: Asking price when transfer-listing, x v_high. 1.0 when we want to sell: the top of the valuation is what a buyer will pay, and a listed player already draws lower bids (user, 2026-10-08). asking_price_deter (fm sell --deter) only for players listed but not really for sale. first_counter is for answering bids, not for listing.
selling._price_book: fm sell (no --price) reads the live value range, records our minimum and target in local/runs/price-book.json (analysis/evaluate_offer.py --price; minimum never below minimum_vs_v_low x v_low, target never below v_high) and lists the player with asking price Unspecified (user, 2026-10-08). Bids for a player in the price book: accept if guaranteed >= minimum, counter towards target (at most max_counters), reject below minimum once counters are spent; lowballs rejected. Asking prices (--price, --deter) only when re-pricing an already-listed player.
selling._keep: fm sell refuses (keep him) when our minimum exceeds this x v_high: the analysis says he is worth more to us than the market pays (McKnight: range 24K-200K, replacing his output costs ~11M). --min overrides.
selling._loans: Loan offers for our players (user, 2026-10-08): with an OBLIGATION to buy, it is a sale: guaranteed = loan fee + monthly fees over the loan + obligation fee, decided like a transfer bid (price-book minimum if listed). Never reject only because it is a loan. With only an OPTION to buy (e.g. Valdimarsson: 1.8M after 25 games, optional): a plain loan, decided on wage relief and depth (escalate).
selling._list_players: User (2026-10-09), after listing 5-6 first-teamers all season and finishing the first half 19th: do NOT transfer-list players (it hurts morale and ships the first team out). Consider bids as they come: every bid is judged against our Moneyball minimum for that player (evaluate_offer.py --price on the bid's value range), keep him when he is worth more to us than the market pays. fm sell only with --force.

agent_payoff._payoff: Fractions of the agent's first ask. Always settle: counter at counter_at, then accept any reply at or below accept_at_or_below (user rule, 2026-10-04).

buying._raise: Each raise adds this x v_low.
buying._max: x v_high unless the analyst sets a walk-away maximum first.

escalate._about: Situations where the loop stops for analysis instead of a handler.

contracts._salary_factors: Personal terms for signings: keep the agent's bonuses/clauses, offer this share of the demanded salary in turn (user rule: agents give a little on salary, are firm on the rest).
contracts._max_salary: Personal terms: accept a demand up to this x our FIRST-TEAM median wage (top 25 earners, analysis/wage_bands.py; ~£51K in July 2026), negotiating via salary_factors; above it, stop for a decision. The contract screen's 'Avg.' includes youth/reserves (squad median £7K) and is no longer used (user, 2026-10-08: Camara's £36-44.5K is a normal first-team wage).
